segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics digest from October 26, 2026.
We cover 17 top stories, including the robotaxi race in Europe, Toyota's humanoid factory push, and new funding for personal vertical flight.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Arthur D. Little consultant: Europe emerging as battleground for global robotaxi race"
reports on the emergence of Europe as a crucial battleground for the global robotaxi race due to its relative openness compared to the United States and China.
This fragmentation creates opportunities for robotaxi companies seeking an early market foothold by allowing direct competition between Chinese and Western firms.
Success in Europe is contingent upon vehicle economics, fleet utilization, regulation, consumer trust, and the ability to operate profitably at scale.
Markets such as Spain and the United Kingdom present distinct opportunities based on regulatory timing and market size.
Fleet operators who can optimize vehicle utilization and costs are anticipated to be the long-term winners in this competitive landscape.
This development signals that regulatory environments and operational efficiency will determine market success for autonomous ride-sharing services.
From Humanoid.guide, "Toyota humanoid strategy targets factories in robotics push".
This report details Toyota's plan to invest six point four billion dollars annually in factory automation by deploying four hundred thousand robots to commercialize robotics research.
The strategy centers on automating factory work and mitigating labor shortages rather than focusing on external robot markets initially.
Toyota is utilizing its internally developed Eley humanoid, which learns tasks by observing factory workers through an in-house foundation model.
The company prioritizes integrating robots, artificial intelligence, and production processes into a unified operating system as a core competitive advantage.
Deployment will initially focus on internal factories, with projections estimating Toyota could secure a small portion of the humanoid market by twenty thirty five.
This development signals a focus on practical industrial application for advanced humanoid robotics within manufacturing sectors.
From Robotics & Automation News, "eVTOL company Skyfly lands $10 million to bring personal vertical flight to market".
This report details the successful securing of a ten million dollar seed round for Skyfly Technologies to advance its electric aircraft development.

The funding was led by HICO Investment Group and Archangel and is allocated to complete the certification process for the Axe, a two-seat electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, and to expand production capabilities.
The Axe design adheres to updated FAA Light Sport Aircraft rules, emphasizing an aerodynamically efficient and cost-effective structure.

Furthermore, the company is concurrently developing the Longbow, a hybrid-electric unmanned aircraft intended for defense and logistics sectors, building upon extensive prototype flight testing and a defined customer pipeline.
This development indicates continued progression in the commercial viability of personal air mobility technologies.

From Robotics & Automation News, Schaeffler opened a state-of-the-art lighthouse factory in Taicang, China, dedicated to humanoid robotics, demonstrating a closed manufacturing loop where humanoids assemble key joint modules for other humanoids.
This facility incorporates an intelligent assembly line and a training center designed to facilitate the mass production of humanoid robot components.
The operation utilizes manufacturing expertise combined with physical AI and digital twins for testing and optimizing production processes.

The factory functions by having humanoids assemble essential joint modules, which subsequently feeds into the production of other humanoids, effectively creating a self-sustaining manufacturing ecosystem.
This initiative seeks to accelerate the adoption of humanoids in industry by advancing the entire humanoid robotics development sphere.
This development signals a significant step toward industrializing humanoid robotics through advanced manufacturing integration.
From Robohub, "Robots in Society, Business and Culture: September 2026"
reports on the advancement and integration of robotics across various sectors, with industrial robot installations reaching over five million globally in 2026, led by China.
Research is also progressing in the development of anthropomorphic robotic hands capable of self-supported locomotion and manipulation through reinforcement learning.
Investigations in India indicate that women are being compensated to record household tasks to facilitate the training of these robots on real-world manipulation scenarios.
Discussions continue regarding the regulation and potential prohibition of autonomous weapons systems.
Studies further suggest that perceived fairness, concerning both distributive and informational aspects, can positively influence the acceptance of security robots.
This progress indicates ongoing development in human-robot interaction and the evolving legal frameworks surrounding autonomous technologies.
From The Robot Report, Teradyne Robotics partners with Sereact to scale physical AI in retail and logistics.
This story details a collaboration aimed at advancing physical artificial intelligence solutions for retail and logistics through integrated robotics.
Sereact's Cortex platform utilizes Universal Robots robot arms to automate unstructured tasks such as handling returns and picking within fulfillment operations.
The combined technology enables a single intelligent system to manage diverse tasks involving mixed goods and varied packaging across multiple robotic units.
This integrated solution is currently operational in Zalando's fulfillment centers across Europe for the processing of returned fashion items.
The joint effort seeks to expand these AI-powered automation methods across numerous global industries.
This development signifies a tangible step toward deploying complex physical AI systems in real-world commercial environments.
Future developments will focus on the global scalability of this integrated automation technology.
From Robotics & Automation News, advasolutions automates logistics center of drugstore chain Hebe in Poland.
This report details the implementation of a tote-based storage system for the Polish drugstore chain Hebe, involving the deployment of autonomous shuttles to manage inventory.
The project entails retrofitting an existing building with sixty-six autonomous advaShuttles designed to store approximately twenty thousand totes at ten meters high.

The implementation proceeds in phases during ongoing operations with a planned go-live in early 2028, integrating the system with SAP EWM and incorporating automated replenishment and conveyor technology for discrepancy handling.
This methodology demonstrates the capability of modular automation to be integrated into live operational environments without requiring major structural alterations.
The project signals continued progression in applying modular automation solutions across complex retail logistics.
From Humanoid.guide, AgiBot Expedition A3 sets a dance record with 110 humanoid robots.
This report details the achievement of a Guinness World Record for the most humanoid robots dancing simultaneously, accomplished in Jinan, China, on October 24, 2026.

The performance involved the coordinated movement of one hundred and ten machines utilizing AgiBot’s LinkBots cluster control and ultra wideband positioning technology to achieve centimeter-level accuracy during complex maneuvers including repositioning, jumps, and flips.
This demonstration emphasized fleet coordination rather than industrial productivity, showcasing the technical challenge of synchronizing motion among numerous mobile machines.
Future applications for this technology are anticipated in areas such as cultural performances, public services, and education.
This achievement indicates significant progress in large-scale robotic coordination capabilities.
From Humanoid.guide, the ETH Zurich team demonstrates Unitree G1 climbing and crawling.
This report details the development of a single policy enabling the robot to walk, climb, and crawl without manual scripting of transitions.
The research involved training the system using thirteen point two minutes of human motion data to learn contact patterns.
Reinforcement learning within simulation was then employed to enable the robot to adapt to novel terrains.
During operation, onboard sensing and a goal guide the robot's movements, eliminating the need for reference motion during transitions.
The team successfully demonstrated climbing, including a ladder recovery, utilizing the learned policy instead of explicitly programmed sequences.
This advancement signifies progress in developing generalized locomotion skills for robotic systems.
Further research will focus on expanding the adaptability of these learned policies across diverse environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, beRobox unveils advanced palletizer featuring ‘3D dynamic safety’.
This report details the introduction of a dynamic safety system for PALTZ robotic palletizers that adapts to the workspace in real time.
The system incorporates a 3D dynamic safety module utilizing Sonair's safety-certified ADAR One 3D ultrasonic sensor to achieve three-dimensional detection of people and objects.
This capability allows the safety system to adjust dynamically to the palletizing workspace, permitting safe operator access during operations.

The technology enables more selective responses to operator interactions without halting the entire cell and maintains presence detection around the robot to prevent unintended restarts when an area is occupied.
This advancement points toward increased integration of advanced sensing for safer and more adaptable industrial automation environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, "The Air Behind the Robot: Why Compressed Air Piping Decides How Well an Automated Line Runs"
reports on how the quality and pressure of compressed air supply directly affect the operation of pneumatic components in automated lines.
Inadequate air delivery results in extended cycle times and part slippage, frequently causing maintenance difficulties that are difficult to isolate.
The research details that leaks, corrosion resulting from moisture, and the material selections within the piping network significantly influence the long-term reliability of the system.
Effective air distribution necessitates meticulous leak detection and careful material selection to mitigate production losses.
Modern design approaches incorporate flexible loop systems and quick-connect fittings to allow for plant modifications while preserving system integrity.
This emphasis on infrastructure quality is crucial for the continued reliable deployment of advanced automation technologies.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, TRON 2!".
This segment details the specifications and capabilities of the TRON 2, a modular embodied robot developed by LimX Dynamics that functions as a research and prototyping tool.
The robot measures one hundred thirty-two centimeters and weighs thirty-five kilograms, offering configurable forms such as dual arm, bipedal, or wheeled legs.
It possesses a maximum speed of eighteen kilometers per hour and supports functionalities including obstacle avoidance, stair walking, and goods sorting.
The system is built upon a Linux-based framework incorporating ROS and features for virtual reality teleoperation.
Furthermore, the robot has a skill score of four out of ten, suggesting a current strength in mobility over manipulation tasks.
This advancement indicates ongoing development in embodied robotics and teleoperated systems.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, StarBot Astra!".

This report details the introduction of StarBot Astra, a humanoid research platform designed for embodied robotics investigation in supervised settings, demonstrating capabilities in obstacle avoidance and sorting goods.

The platform measures one hundred fifty-two centimeters in height and weighs thirty-four kilograms, incorporating twenty-three degrees of freedom and electric joints, along with hands featuring five fingers.
It operates on a Linux and ROS software environment utilizing an NVIDIA Jetson Orin system, facilitating research into practical robotic tasks.
Preliminary assessments indicate that the system functions as a preliminary research system rather than a mature general-purpose worker.
This development signals ongoing investigation into the practical application and limitations of embodied robotics research.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Linker Hand L20!".
This report details the specifications and features of the Linker Hand L20 robotic hand, which achieves a Humanoid.Guide Hand Score of six out of ten, suggesting a design emphasis on dexterity.
The mechanical design of the Linker Hand L20 incorporates five fingers and weighs approximately one point two kilograms.
Movement is facilitated by brushless motors and a rigid linkage transmission system.
The device operates across a voltage range of twenty-four to forty-eight volts and supports communication via CAN or RS485 interfaces.
The hand is currently listed as in production with an advertised price of four thousand two hundred US dollars.
This development indicates ongoing advancement in the integration of complex mechanical dexterity into robotic systems.
Further developments in articulated robotics are anticipated in the near future.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Tau Humanoid!".

This segment details the introduction of the Tau Humanoid, a robot designed for home and office cleaning, demonstrating capabilities in tasks such as obstacle avoidance, sorting goods, and folding clothes.
The robot measures one hundred thirty-two centimeters in height and weighs thirty-five kilograms, constructed from aluminum alloy and engineering plastics.
It operates with artificial intelligence assistance and remote human guidance rather than full autonomy.
Skill scores indicate stronger manipulation performance than navigation ability.
Tau Robotics offers the robot through a cleaning service, necessitating remote human supervision for all operations.
This development points toward advancements in hybrid robotic systems integrating fine motor skills with navigation capabilities.
Further developments in remote human-robot interaction are anticipated within the technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, RH5MK1!".
This segment reports on the specifications and performance of the RH5MK1, a dexterous robotic hand manufactured by Inspire Robotics in China, which achieved an overall score of nine out of ten.
The hand received a rating of five out of five for Degrees of Freedom and four out of five for Strength, emphasizing its high level of dexterity in robotic hand design.
This dual rating system allows for a comparative assessment between dexterity and strength in robotic hand selection.
The RH5MK1 is currently in production and is advertised with a price of fifteen thousand United States dollars.
This development provides a measurable benchmark for evaluating the trade-offs between fine motor control and physical strength in advanced robotic manipulators.
The ongoing production of this model indicates continued advancement in the field of sophisticated robotic hardware.
From Hackaday - Robots, "Hairy Armor For Combat Robot? It’s Not Terrible!".

This story details an experiment investigating the feasibility of using bristles as lightweight, impact-resistant armor for combat robots, with the finding that the hairy design successfully withstood impacts that fractured the outer shells of prior robots.
The experiment involved a robot competing in a plastic antweight division where the concept was tested.
The robot's hairy exterior demonstrated resilience against impacts, suggesting the concept holds potential for combat robotics designs.
The experimentation was facilitated by the use of three-dimensional printing to enable the creation of these unorthodox robot designs.
This research indicates that novel surface structures can contribute to enhanced protection in robotic systems.
Future development should explore the application of such material science in advanced defense technologies.
And that's all the circuits for today, October 26th, 2026.
From autonomous rides to the European robotaxi battle, keep those algorithms running smoothly.
Thanks for plugging into the future with me.
See you next time!
